verdict.rationale: Jules lets a developer assign a reported GitHub issue to an agent with the "jules" label. It then clones the repo in a VM, generates a plan, modifies files and opens a PR, and its API is documented for automating bug fixing. Hands-on reports are mixed: some users fixed errors and got usable PRs, while others needed back-and-forth fixes and found it weak beyond simple problems. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of autonomous bug diagnosis or root-cause analysis (as opposed to generic task execution), independent evidence of reliable unattended fixes on complex codebases, and PR auto-creation off by default via the API.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent autonomously diagnose and fix a reported bug

citations.quote: Use the "jules" label in an issue to assign a task directly in GitHub.
Jules runs in a virtual machine where it clones your code, installs dependencies, and modifies files.
Jules creates a PR of the changes.
automate tasks like bug fixing and code reviews
It failed the first time, I gave it the error message and it fixed it.
